title: Fuzzing-Inspired Adversarial Prompt Generation for Safety Evals

novelty_assessment.reasoning: Multiple mature frameworks already exist: LLM-Fuzzer (USENIX Security 2024) scales jailbreak assessment using fuzzing, PROMPTFUZZ (2024) directly applies fuzzing techniques to prompt generation, Palo Alto Unit42 published coverage-guided prompt fuzzing results across open/closed models, and an in-browser LLM-guided fuzzing framework for prompt injection testing was published in 2025. The core idea of applying coverage-guided fuzzing to adversarial prompt generation for safety evaluation is well-explored with published tools and benchmarks.

title: Differential Item Functioning Analysis for Demographic Bias in Safety Evals

title: Interrater Reliability Standards for Human Safety Annotations

title: Test-Retest Reliability of Safety Benchmarks Under Temperature Variation

The proposed study is essentially already completed.

title: Norm Referencing vs. Criterion Referencing for AI Safety Thresholds

title: Process Capability Indices for Continuous Safety Monitoring

title: Prospective vs. Retrospective Safety Evaluation Design

novelty_assessment.reasoning: The general problem of prospective vs retrospective evaluation is well-discussed in medical AI (only 2% of ML health studies are prospective), and the need for pre-registration in AI research is recognized. The concept is discussed as a need but not experimentally demonstrated for AI safety.

title: Dose-Response Curves for Harmful Capability Elicitation

novelty_assessment.reasoning: While capability elicitation guidelines exist (METR), refusal rate analysis is active, and research shows many 'nearby' prompts elicit the same behavior, no published work was found that explicitly applies the dose-response curve framework with graded prompt aggressiveness scales to characterize safety profiles. RefusalBench and similar work measure binary refusal rates but do not model the continuous dose-response relationship. The pharmacological framing is a novel contribution.

title: Ecological Validity Assessment for Safety Benchmarks

novelty_assessment.reasoning: The 'sociotechnical gap' between benchmark evaluation and real-world deployment is well-documented. 'How Should AI Safety Benchmarks Benchmark Safety?' While the problem is well-characterized, a systematic empirical comparison between benchmark predictions and real-world safety behavior using deployment data has not been published.

title: Causal Chain Decomposition of Benchmark Contamination to Deployment Harm

novelty_assessment.reasoning: Benchmark contamination is extensively studied with surveys (arxiv 2406.04244, 2502.14425), controlled contamination experiments showing 5-15% accuracy distortion, and multiple mitigation strategies (AntiLeakBench, watermarking). The causal chain from contamination to inflated scores is well-documented. However, the specific decomposition tracing contamination through to deployment harm via safety-specific benchmarks, identifying which causal link is weakest, has not been the focus of published work. The contamination side is largely addressed; the deployment harm side is novel.

title: Intervention Points in the Sandbagging Causal Chain

novelty_assessment.reasoning: AI sandbagging is now well-studied following the landmark paper 'AI Sandbagging: Language Models can Strategically Underperform on Evaluations' (ICLR 2025, arxiv 2406.07358). The phenomenon is established but the intervention framework is newer.

title: Breaking the Chain: When Does Eval Failure Translate to Deployment Harm?

novelty_assessment.reasoning: While the evaluation-deployment gap is acknowledged in the literature, and causal Bayesian networks for safety analysis exist (arxiv 2505.19860), no published work was found that builds an explicit probabilistic causal model mapping evaluation failures to deployment harms specifically for AI safety. The 81% of benchmarks evaluating only predefined risks and 79% reducing safety to binary pass/fail (from a 2025 survey) highlight the gap this would address. The Bayesian network approach to this specific question is novel.

title: The False Negative Causal Chain: Unsafe Models Passing Safety Evals
